title: Planar polar integration with an arbitrary center
statement: Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field], planar Lebesgue measure $dA$, product Lebesgue measure $dr\,d\theta$, and $T=(0,\infty)\times(-\pi,\pi)$. For every $c\in\mathbf C$ and every function $f:\mathbf C\to[0,\infty]$, the extended nonnegative Lebesgue integrals satisfy $$\int_{\mathbf C}^{-}f(w)\,dA(w)=\int_T^{-}r\,f(c+re^{i\theta})\,dr\,d\theta.$$ For every Lebesgue integrable $h:\mathbf C\to\mathbf C$, $$\int_{\mathbf C}h(w)\,dA(w)=\int_T r\,h(c+re^{i\theta})\,dr\,d\theta.$$ Extended nonnegative integration is defined without an integrability hypothesis.
